svg.title: DDIA 4 · ENCODING & EVOLUTION: sketchnote
svg.text: Data outlives code. During a rolling deploy, old and new versions
of your service run at the same time, reading each other's data.
v1 updates the name and writes the whole object back, and
phone is gone. Old code must preserve unknown fields.
Breaking changes: required fields, renumbering tags, or changing
a type in an incompatible way.
Messages: the sender doesn't wait. A broker buffers, retries,
and fans out. Producer and consumer evolve independently, so
a schema registry keeps them compatible.
"How do you deploy schema changes with zero downtime?"
Expand → migrate → contract: add the nullable column, deploy code that writes both, backfill, switch reads, and only then drop the old column.
"How do Kafka producers and consumers evolve?"
Avro or Protobuf with a schema registry enforcing backward-compatible changes. Consumers upgrade on their own schedule.
gRPC (Protobuf, HTTP/2) for internal high-QPS calls; REST/JSON for public APIs and browsers.
"Every message carries a schema version, and we only add optional fields. That lets the booking service deploy without coordinating with its consumers."
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.
